paragraphs: Rabbah bar Shilat, Gittin 39b, according to the reading of the Bach.
Rav Shmuel bar Shilat: [Shabbat 153a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.153a.2). Shilat’s grandson Rav Yehudah: [Berakhot 47a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.47a.4).

And in the [Shitah Mekubbetzet on Ketubot 62a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shita_Mekubetzet_on_Ketubot.62a.9), it is cited in the name of Rabbenu Hai Gaon that Shilat is a feminine name: the sister of Rabbi Chiyya.[^2]

notes.text: The William Davidson vocalized text of Berakhot 47a explicitly names Rav Yehudah as Rav Shmuel bar Shilat’s son, consistent with the notice calling him Shilat’s grandson. The explanation that Shilat is a woman, Rabbi Chiya’s sister, is attributed to Rabbenu Hai Gaon in Shitah Mekubetzet.

The linked Shitah assigns the identification of Shilat as Shmuel’s mother and Rabbi Chiyya’s sister to Rabbenu Hai Gaon; its neighboring glosses are distinct. The linked Berakhot gives Rav Yehudah son of Rav Shmuel bar Shilat transmitting in Rav’s name. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3296&lang=en) reports the maternal interpretation but disputes it.
